tagline: Detect the filter context state — make measures that behave differently depending on how they are sliced

slides.title: Context Detection Functions
slides.body: HASONEVALUE and ISFILTERED let your DAX measures check the current filter context and change their behavior accordingly. HASONEVALUE returns TRUE if a column has exactly one value in the current filter context (only one item selected). ISFILTERED returns TRUE if a column has any direct filter applied to it. These are the foundation of conditional measures — showing a subtotal when no selection is made, or displaying 'Select one product' when multiple are selected.
slides.keyPoint: HASONEVALUE(column) = exactly one unique value is visible in the current context. ISFILTERED(column) = at least one filter has been directly applied to the column. They answer different questions about the filter context.

slides.title: Filter Context Scenarios
slides.caption: How each function behaves depending on slicer state
slides.note: ISFILTERED detects DIRECT filters only. A cross-filter from another table (e.g., Region slicer filtering via relationship) does NOT make ISFILTERED return TRUE on the filtered table's column.

slides.title: Conditional Measure Patterns
slides.code:
-- Pattern 1: Show a specific value only when one product is selected
Single Product Revenue =
IF(
    HASONEVALUE(DimProduct[ProductName]),
    [Total Revenue],
    "Select exactly one product"
)

-- Pattern 2: Show selected value or a default message
Selected Region =
IF(
    HASONEVALUE(DimRegion[Region]),
    SELECTEDVALUE(DimRegion[Region]),
    "All Regions"
)

-- Pattern 3: Change metric when category is filtered
Dynamic KPI =
IF(
    ISFILTERED(DimProduct[Category]),
    [Category Revenue Share %],
    [Total Revenue]
)

-- Pattern 4: Check if MULTIPLE items are selected
MultiSelect Warning =
IF(
    ISFILTERED(DimProduct[ProductKey]) && NOT HASONEVALUE(DimProduct[ProductKey]),
    "⚠ Multiple products selected",
    BLANK()
)
slides.annotation: Pattern 4 combines ISFILTERED (something is selected) with NOT HASONEVALUE (more than one thing selected) to detect a multi-select state — useful for warning users when a metric only makes sense for a single selection.

slides.title: Result — Context-Aware Measure Behavior
slides.caption: The same measure produces different output depending on slicer state
slides.note: Context-detection functions are most useful for card visuals and KPI tiles where showing a company-wide total alongside a per-product detail would be confusing.

slides.title: HASONEVALUE vs SELECTEDVALUE vs ISINSCOPE
bullets: HASONEVALUE(col) → TRUE/FALSE — 'Is exactly one value in context?'
SELECTEDVALUE(col, [alternate]) → returns the single value or alternate — combines HASONEVALUE check internally
ISFILTERED(col) → TRUE/FALSE — 'Has a direct filter been applied to this column?'
ISCROSSFILTERED(col) → TRUE/FALSE — 'Is this column filtered directly OR through a relationship?'
ISINSCOPE(col) → TRUE/FALSE — 'Is this column at a visible level in a matrix subtotal hierarchy?'
slides.keyPoint: SELECTEDVALUE(col, 'All') is shorthand for IF(HASONEVALUE(col), VALUES(col), 'All'). Use it when you want the single selected value or a fallback. Use HASONEVALUE when you need a boolean condition for more complex logic.

slides.title: PL-300 Exam — Key Facts
bullets: HASONEVALUE checks the filter context, not the visual rendering — it evaluates at the data engine level
ISFILTERED(col) = TRUE only for DIRECT filters on the column; cross-filters from relationships return FALSE
ISCROSSFILTERED(col) = TRUE for both direct and indirect (relationship) filters — use this to detect filters from related tables

Common exam scenario: 'A card visual should show total revenue when no product is selected, or product-specific revenue when one is selected' → IF(HASONEVALUE(Product[Name]), [Product Revenue], [Total Revenue])
SELECTEDVALUE is the most concise solution for single-selection display — the exam often rewards using it over a verbose IF/HASONEVALUE construct
slides.keyPoint: HASONEVALUE = context guard. ISFILTERED = filter detection. SELECTEDVALUE = context-aware display. Know when to use each — and remember ISFILTERED only detects direct filters, not cross-filter propagation.
